title: Interim (C:contained-swimmers): the crawler's self-made layer sweeps an excluded cargo along through motion; the matched no-exclusion twin leaves it behind
summary: world2.py = the layer crawler of 20261025T2349-c31-crawler-layer-sighting plus a cargo c made inside the body (kc=0.1, decay 0.05) with chemical potential ln c + kappa*s, i.e. excluded by the cell's own layer species s (Scharfetter-Gummel face flux, Dc=0.05). With kappa=10 the cargo in/out ratio (signed distance, inside sd<-0.1 vs 0.1<sd<0.4) stays 8.5-14 on seeds 0-1 for t=1-12, and 5-8 on the rear side, where the retracting rim sweeps the cargo forward so it piles up just inside the rear rim (koff_cmp.png). With kappa=0 (same production) the ratio is ~2 overall only because the front advances onto clean ground, 1.0-1.3 at the rear, and the cell holds 32-51% of its cargo vs 80-84%. Carrying test (seed 1, cargo production off at t=6): with the layer the cell keeps in/out 3.9-6 for the next 12 time units while crawling ~3 diameters (cargo 0.355 -> 0.11, against 0.195 for pure decay, so it leaks ~5%/time); without exclusion the ratio drops below 1 within 1.5 time units. Layer-source ablation (SRC=none, labkit seeds 0-1, pack_nosrc): the cell crawls as far (5.0-5.1 body lengths), s is flat zero and c is not membrane-like (rim/core 0.91), so the layer does work on contents, not on motion.

finding.operator: exclusion of a cargo by the cell's own adsorbed layer species (cargo potential ln c + kappa s)
finding.control: matched ablation kappa=0 (same cargo production) and layer-source ablation SRC=none
finding.result: in/out 8.5-14 (rear 5-8) vs ~2 (rear 1.0-1.3); held 80-84% vs 32-51%; after production off ratio 3.9-6 for 12 t vs <1 within 1.5 t
